speaker: Melody
teaser: Her right ear woke up muffled. She's waiting for it to pop.
hello: Hi! Melody Belle. I teach music at the primary school, and I run the kids' choir.
Two days ago I woke up and my right ear felt stuffed with cotton wool. And it's ringing.
It'll pop on its own, won't it? Our spring concert is on Friday.

which_ear.say: The right, no question. Like someone stuffed a sock in it. The left is perfect.
which_ear.note: Right ear muffled, left ear fine

say: All of a sudden! Two days ago I went to bed fine and woke up like this.
Like a door slammed shut overnight. It hasn't budged since.
onset.note: Sudden: woke up with it 2 days ago

ringing.say: Yes, a high ringing, right ear only. It started the same morning. Like a triangle nobody will put down.

say: No pain, nothing leaking, no spinning. Not even a wobble.
It just feels full, like when a plane lands. But I haven't been on a plane.
red_flags.note: No pain, drainage or dizziness; ear feels full

say: Thirty kids with recorders, every single day. Does that count?
But nothing new. No concert, no bang. Just a normal week of Hot Cross Buns.
noise.note: Noisy classroom; no loud bang lately

ear_history.say: Never! No infections, no operations, no knocks. And it's never done this before.
ear_history.note: No ear trouble ever; never happened before

family.say: Not that I know of. My gran sang in the church choir till she was ninety.
family.note: No hearing loss in the family

health.say: Healthy! No medicines, no cold, not even a sniffle. Just honey lozenges for my singing voice.

aids.say: Never. Until two days ago I had perfect ears. Nearly perfect pitch, too.

say: Choir practice. I can't tell where the altos are any more.
And the piano sounds a bit sour on my right side. For a music teacher, that's a nightmare.
hardest.note: Can't place voices; piano sounds off on right

right.caption: Melody's RIGHT ear: a narrow, clean canal and a shiny, healthy eardrum. No wax, no fluid in sight.

left.caption: Melody's LEFT ear: narrow and clean too, with a pearly eardrum. A perfect match.

tymp.note: Tymp: type A both ears, no fluid

decision_lines.fit: Hold the hearing aids! A loss that arrived overnight needs a doctor first, and today.
decision_lines.refer: Right idea, wrong speed. A normal referral takes days or weeks. A sudden loss can't wait.
decision_lines.today: Doctor TODAY! A sudden loss in one ear is urgent, pain or no pain. Early treatment works best.
decision_lines.clear: No aids needed? Her right ear needs 45 to 65 dB. And it changed overnight: doctor today!

why.prompt: Why does Melody see a doctor TODAY?
options: It came on overnight, and her bone is down too.
Right! Sudden, one ear, and deeper than wax or fluid: a doctor the same day.
Her right ear is much worse than her left.
True, and that alone means refer. What makes it TODAY is how fast it came.
Her full ear means fluid behind the eardrum.
Her tymp was type A: no fluid. A full feeling often comes with a sudden loss.
Ringing in one ear is an emergency.
One-sided ringing is a red flag, but alone it means refer. The sudden loss makes it today.

debrief: A sudden loss in one ear is an emergency, even with no pain. Treatment works best early.
A full, blocked feeling is often the first sign. Her normal tymp said it wasn't fluid.
One ear much worse? Mask its bone and air: the good ear may be answering for it.
goodbye: Hoot at Booth Camp. Sudden loss in her right ear, two days ago. Can you see her today?
Four o'clock? Wonderful. Her chart is on its way to you now.
Melody, the ear doctor sees you at four. Go straight there. Rehearsal can wait.
Straight there. But what if it doesn't come back?
Many sudden losses get better, some all the way. Either way, come back afterwards: we retest and help.
And if your face goes numb or droopy, or your speech slurs: emergency department, straight away.
Doctor at four. And on Friday, the altos stand on my left!

headlines.S: MELODY'S EAR HITS A SOUR NOTE; DOCTOR TODAY
headlines.A: NO TIME FOR A REST: TEACHER SEES DOCTOR TODAY
headlines.B: MELODY SENT IN TEMPO; A FEW STAMPS OFF-KEY
headlines.C: SUDDEN EAR CAUGHT, BUT THE CHART SANG FLAT
headlines.Do-over: OWL CALLS REHEARSAL; MELODY ALREADY AT DOCTOR

subheads.S: Overnight, one ear, bone down with the air: a doctor the same day, concert or not.
subheads.A: A sudden loss in one ear is urgent even without pain, and early treatment works best.
subheads.B: The right call at the right speed, though a few stamps drifted off the stave.
subheads.C: When one ear is much worse, mask its bone and air before you trust the chart.
subheads.Do-over: A full ear that arrives overnight means a doctor today; the choir will wait.
